reading.body:
CyrusOne's Aurora campus, with 114 MW of IT capacity across three collocated facilities, can house approximately 2,850 AI training racks at standard density, making it sufficient for meaningful training clusters but not hyperscale frontier installations.

The campus represents 48 percent of Illinois's publicly disclosed data center capacity, yet this state-level share obscures two limitations. Forty-four of the 50 mapped Illinois facilities publish no capacity figures, making the true distribution of infrastructure invisible. Illinois's total published capacity of 236 MW ranks it far behind leading AI hub states, suggesting the region has not yet consolidated the power and real estate density that AI scaling requires.

The gap between published specifications and operational reality is substantial. CyrusOne discloses IT capacity and technical space, but power availability at the Aurora site, grid interconnection capacity, tenant occupancy, and power purchase terms remain undisclosed. These factors determine whether the facility can actually support the density its footprint suggests or whether upgrades to local power infrastructure are the binding constraint on AI workload placement.
